messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (p99 > 2.5s for 12m). root_thread_ts=2071002222

anjali (oncall): i'm on it. p95/p99 both climbing. looks like streaming stalls, clients timing out. any infra noise?

mike (infra): no deploys in the last 90m. telemetry shows a small set of GPU hosts with thermal throttle spikes and ECC corrected counts rising ~2071002000-2071002150. sending node diagnostics.

infra-bot: node-gpu-21: ECC_CORRECTED=28; thermal_throttle=1; temp=88C; fan=82%

sarah (runtime): when those nodes get KV cache misses + long context requests, jobs block in gpu-queue longer than usual. that yields streaming tail stalls. suspect hardware-induced slowdowns/backpressure.

anjali (oncall): mitigation options: 1) immediate traffic diversion away from affected pool-thermal, 2) reduce streaming max_tokens per session, 3) enable lightweight-model fallback for requests hitting bad nodes. i'd like 1 now and 3 as a safety net.

mike (infra): applying route change: prefer pool-cool (us-west-2) for streaming for 20m. command: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --service=streaming --prefer-pool=pool-cool --ttl=1200
```

mike (infra): route change applied. monitoring rebalancing of pods.

anjali (oncall): lowering continuous_batch_max on pool-thermal to 6 to reduce head-of-line delays.

sarah (runtime): batch cap applied. also flipping on a runtime guard to abort streaming sessions with >30s of no-progress to avoid hung streams. low-risk config roll.

carla (support): two paying customers reported interrupted streams (acct-309 and acct-911). i've sent immediate notifications and an interim status.

mike (infra): starting cordon/drain for node-gpu-21. cmds: 
```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-21
kubectl drain node-gpu-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
infra-bot: drain started for node-gpu-21; evicted_pods=10; streaming-workers=4

james (oncall-next): i'll take hardware lead. plan: cordon+drain (in flight), collect nvdiag and ECC histograms, then repro on spare if possible. ETA 20m.

mike (infra): nvdiag snapshot requested. pushing logs to /artifacts/incidents/2071002222/

vendor-bot: created vendor ticket VT-4892 (severity=high). contact: hw-support@vendor.com.

anjali (oncall): summary for now: likely flaky GPU (ECC corrections) causing thermal events -> scheduler/backpressure -> streaming p99 spike. mitigations = routing pref to pool-cool, batch cap, runtime abort guard, node drain.

james (oncall-next): after drain completes i'll try to repro the ECC pattern on a spare card. if persistent, request hot-swap. will keep thread updated.

carla (support): drafting customer-facing note: "We detected streaming interruptions tied to a subset of GPU infrastructure. We've rerouted traffic and are replacing affected hardware. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Want me to send now?

james (oncall-next): yes, send interim and say ETA for hardware replacement pending vendor response. include ticket VT-4892.

anjali (oncall): also logging the config changes and timeline. create the postmortem stub: /docs/incidents/2071002222-postmortem.md (assigned: james, sarah, mike, carla).

mike (infra): quick metrics: before mitigations p99=3.4s, p95=1.3s. ten minutes after reroute p99=1.8s, p95=0.9s. trending down but still watching tail.

infra-bot: health-check: pool-thermal avg_temp=85.7C; pool-cool avg_temp=70.2C.

sarah (runtime): enabling fallback policy for requests hitting nodes with ECC_CORRECTED>15 or thermal_throttle==1: route to model-v1-slim. snippet: 
```
fallback_policies:
  - condition: ECC_CORRECTED > 15 OR thermal_throttle == 1
    action: route_to: model-v1-slim
```

anjali (oncall): good. also add a canary plan for when we move traffic back to pool-thermal. we need a slow ramp and p99 watch. tag @sarah @mike for canary.

james (oncall-next): drain finished. collected nvdiag and dmesg. pushing artifacts and ECC histogram to /artifacts/incidents/2071002222/diagnostics.tar.gz. initial look: kernel logged corrected ECC bursts +/- memory controller ECC interrupts.

vendor-bot: vendor responded: "acknowledged — replacement parts on order, on-site window TBD 48-72h. advise hot-swap if available." ticket VT-4892 updated.

carla (support): customers updated with vendor ticket ref and mitigation summary. both asked for estimated recovery; told them 48-72h for replacement but streaming is restored via routing and fallback.

anjali (oncall): handing active incident to james for postmortem + vendor coordination. my shift ends in 22m; i'll remain reachable.

james (oncall-next): acknowledged. action items I'm tracking: 1) hardware replacement coordination + hot-swap if possible, 2) improve ECC alert thresholds and automated routing policy, 3) add unit/regression tests for fallback paths to smaller model, 4) document canary rollback steps. will publish draft postmortem by EOD.

infra-bot: monitor update: p95=0.85s, p99=1.6s (down from 3.4s). continuing to monitor 15m windows.

sarah (runtime): follow-up: add a small integration test that simulates ECC-like latency by injecting delayed GPU responses so fallback logic is exercised during CI. putting a ticket in backlog.

carla (support): standing by for final postmortem before sharing with customers.

oncall-bot: Incident 2071002222 - handoff to james completed. severity: elevated -> investigating. thread closed by oncall-bot for active-handoff."
